events.title: Proposed ruling: escalate (model confidence 0.80)
events.body:
This is filed as a safety dispute and the trace settles the SAFE-1 screen as ✓: a safety incident was raised, no automatic ruling is to be made, and the only allowed outcome is escalate [F3][F4]. The chat is complete and every message is timestamped, and it is short — two messages at 21:36 — so the record itself contains no further exchange that would resolve the competing readings of the words in it [F5].

The rider's message asks to be released mid-route: "Please stop the car, I want to get out here." [F3]. The driver's reply is the pivot of the case: "Sit down or I lock the doors." [F4]. Read as written, that sentence conditions the rider's physical release on her compliance and names locking the doors; a message that ties being let out of the moving car to obedience is a statement about confinement, and under SAFE-1 the meaning of the original words is the judge's finding, not the driver's later characterisation [F4][F6]. The driver's statement explains the words as a safety instruction because the rider was allegedly drunk and tried to open the door at the lights on Clemenceau Avenue, and says he did not stop until the destination; that explanation is a post-trip statement, not part of the chat, and it carries no independent record of the alleged door-opening, so it cannot displace the quoted words [F6][F5]. The words are therefore at least capable of being read as a threat of confinement aimed at the passenger — exactly the abuse/intimidation conduct SAFE-1 routes to a human — even though a reviewer might read them as an instruction to remain seated in live traffic [F4][SAFE-1].

The fare and route records give no independent support to either reading and cannot decide a safety complaint: the trip was 15.4 km against an optimal 15.5 km (-0.1 km, -1%) in 20.7 min against a 21.8 min estimate, and the fixed RydeX fare of $32.86 is not in dispute [F1][F2][FARE-1]. Both profiles are clean — the rider has 520 days, 4.8 rating and 0 disputes in 90 days, and the driver 2100 days, 4.9 rating, 1204 trips and 0 disputes/0 upheld in 90 days — and profile facts can never decide a case, so these do not establish or refute the safety allegation [F7][F8][SAFE-1]. There is likewise no GPS or timeline fact recording what happened inside the car at 21:36 or where the car actually stopped, which is precisely why the matter should go to a person rather than be dismissed or refunded here [F1][F5]. No money is ordered because no fare item is shown to be wrongly charged, and escalation — not a refund or no_action — is the outcome the safety screen prescribes [FARE-1][SAFE-1].

Beyond SAFE-1, the dispute type is itself "safety" and the rider's account that she "felt unsafe for the whole ride" is part of the complaint; the safety screen does not turn on any keyword and is to be applied even where a line only hints at a concern, so the conservative course is escalation with a factual summary rather than any automatic outcome [F3][F4][SAFE-1]. The driver's own statement is also not a full denial of the rider's control over the ride: he writes that he "did not stop until the destination" after the request to get out [F3][F6].

ruling.recommended_action: Route to RydeHELP human safety review: read the 21:36 exchange (F3, F4) in context, obtain the driver's account on whether the child-lock was engaged and whether he refused a safe stop, and record the outcome; no refund is due on the fare (fixed RydeX, no deviation).

claims.assertion: The rider asked, in the app at 21:36, to be let out of the moving car: 'Please stop the car, I want to get out here.' (F3).

The driver's reply at the same minute was 'Sit down or I lock the doors.' (F4) — a threat to confine the rider in the vehicle in response to a request to be released; the chat is complete and fully timestamped (F5), so nothing is missing that would explain the words away.

The complaint states the driver threatened to lock the rider in, and the rider says she felt unsafe for the whole ride; the rider has a clean record (520 days, 4.8, 0 disputes in 90 d) (F7), and the only contrary account is the driver's own after-the-fact written statement (F6), which is not part of the chat (F5).

Because the record contains a threat / intimidation allegation, SAFE-1 requires that no automatic ruling be made and that the case be escalated to a human with a fact summary; the rider does not seek to overturn the fixed $32.86 RydeX fare, which the GPS record shows was for a 15.4 km route no longer than the optimal 15.5 km (-1%) (F1) in 20.7 min vs 21.8 min estimated (F2).

The rider reserves the account-review point: the driver's threat to lock the doors is a Code-of-Conduct matter for Ryde to review alongside the escalation, and the 1204 trips in 90 days with 0 prior disputes (F8) is context only, not a defence.

weaknesses: The driver's written statement (F6) gives a safety motive — the rider allegedly tried to open the door at the lights on Clemenceau Avenue — and says he did not stop until the destination; a judge may read 'Sit down or I lock the doors' (F4) as a safety instruction rather than a threat, and the rider's own account of intoxication is not testable from the fact table.

There is no GPS or timeline evidence of a dangerous act (e.g. door opening, hard braking), no timing fact showing when the car actually stopped, and no traffic facts in this case; the rider's case therefore rests on the two chat lines (F3, F4) rather than on any system record of the driving itself.

The route and fare facts (F1, F2) show no deviation and no overcharge, so nothing in the fare record corroborates the rider's account; the profile facts (F7, F8) are clean on both sides and cannot decide this case, and the driver's 1204-trip, 0-dispute record (F8) will be cited against escalation urgency.

claims.assertion: The trip itself shows no route or fare irregularity: actual distance 15.4 km against the optimal 15.5 km (-0.1 km, -1%) and duration 20.7 min against an estimate of 21.8 min, so the fixed $32.86 RydeX fare reflects a shortest-route, on-time trip and nothing in the fare breakdown was inflated by the ride.

The rider's first message was a demand to stop mid-route at 21:36 ('Please stop the car, I want to get out here.'), i.e. in the middle of a carriageway on Clemenceau Avenue rather than at any named or safe stopping place; my client's obligation is to proceed to the destination named by the passenger by the shortest and most direct route.

My client's reply at 21:36 ('Sit down or I lock the doors.') is a request that the rider remain seated while the car was in motion at traffic lights, and the driver statement explains it as for her own safety; on its words it is a safety instruction, not a threat to imprison the rider, and the complaint's paraphrase 'threatened to lock me in' overreads the message.

The whole chat record is two messages, every one timestamped (F5), so there is no missing or untimestamped exchange that could contain any further threat, abuse or harassment beyond the two quoted messages.

The driver stopped at the destination and did not let the rider out mid-carriageway; the record contains no GPS fact, timeline fact or chat message alleging injury, a collision or dangerous driving — the rider's claim is an emotional-safety claim ('I felt unsafe'), which does not by itself establish a traffic accident, personal injury or a dangerous-driving allegation.

My client's record is 5.8 years on the platform, 1204 trips in the last 90 days, rating 4.9, and 0 disputes and 0 upheld disputes (route: 0, no-show: 0), against the rider's 0 disputes in 90 days; there is no pattern of misconduct or abuse in his history to support a flag on his account.

weaknesses: The driver's own message F4 ('Sit down or I lock the doors.') is quoted verbatim in the chat record and is the single strongest piece of evidence against us: a judge reading it as a threat of confinement will trigger SAFE-1 (escalate, no automatic ruling, safety_concern recorded) regardless of the driver's explanation.

The driver's statement F6 admits he 'did not stop until the destination' after the rider asked to get out (F3). The other side will use F3 + F6 to argue he ignored a rider request to stop and overrode her control over the ride, which reads as aggressive even if it is not literally 'locking her in'.

The rider's complaint is a subjective-safety allegation that no system record (F1, F2) can confirm or refute; the absence of a system record of a threat cuts both ways, and the judge may find the meaning of F4 undetermined and escalate rather than dismiss.

My case does not prove the fire doors were unlocked at any moment; I have no gps fact, timeline fact or video showing that, so I cannot positively refute the rider's central assertion from the record — only show the message itself was an instruction, not an act.
F1/F2 show a normal route and time but say nothing about what happened inside the car at 21:36, so they do not rebut the safety complaint and cannot carry the case alone.

points.response: Conceded as far as it goes: F1 and F2 show a 15.4 km route (-1% vs optimal 15.5 km) in 20.7 min vs 21.8 min estimated, so the rider does not contest the $32.86 fixed fare and asks for no money back. This claim does not answer the safety complaint, which concerns what happened inside the car at 21:36 (F4), not the distance driven.

Whether Clemenceau Avenue was 'in the middle of a carriageway' is not in the record: the only source for that road name is the driver's own post-trip statement F6, and no GPS, timeline or route fact places the car there or shows a stop location. RD-1 tells the driver to reach the destination by the shortest route *in the absence of any reasonable cause*; a rider's request to get out at 21:36 (F3) is the situation the driver had to answer, and he answered it in words, not by stopping.

The message must be read as written, not through the driver's later gloss: 'Sit down or I lock the doors.' (F4) conditions the rider's physical release on her compliance, and the word 'lock' is the operative one — 'I lock the doors' is a statement about confinement, not about sitting down. Under SAFE-1 whether it is a threat is for the judge reading the original words, and the driver's own explanation in F6 is a claim, not a record.

Agreed that the chat record is complete and fully timestamped — two messages, both at 21:36 (F5); that is precisely why the driver's own words in F4 are the only account of the 21:36 exchange and cannot be diluted by an untimestamped or missing exchange elsewhere.

The rider's complaint is a threat/intimidation allegation ('the driver threatened to lock me in', 'I felt unsafe'), which SAFE-1 routes to a person; the rider does not allege a collision, injury or dangerous driving and therefore does not invoke SAFE-2. Either way the outcome is escalate, not no_action, because F4 is quoted verbatim in the record and the driver does not deny saying it (F6).

The rider does not ask for flag_account, so this claim is irrelevant to the requested outcome; the profile facts are context only and cannot decide the safety complaint (F7, F8). Note that F8 is also silent on what was said inside the car at 21:36 (F4).

The fact the rider cites (F3) shows only a request to 'get out here' — mid-carriageway at lights on Clemenceau Avenue (F6) — not a threat by my client; her right to ask does not establish the SAFE-1 predicate.

'Sit down or I lock the doors.' (F4) is, on its words, an instruction to remain seated while the vehicle was in motion at traffic lights and my client's statement ties it to opening the door for the rider's own safety (F6); an instruction aimed at preventing a door being opened in live traffic is not intimidation, though I accept the judge may read F4 differently.

The completeness point (F5) is neutral: with only two timestamped messages (F3, F4) there is no other exchange in the record containing any further threat or abuse, and F7 (rider: 520 days, 4.8, 0 disputes) is clean on both sides and cannot decide this case.

I agree escalation is the correct action for a safety alert, but the summary must record that F1 (-0.1 km, -1%) and F2 (-1.1 min) show a normal shortest-route trip, that the only arguable threat is one message (F4) whose stated purpose was preventing a door being opened at lights (F6), and that the driver stopped at the destination as the ride was completed — not the rider's framing; the fare is correctly fixed under FARE-1 and is not in dispute.

A Code-of-Conduct review must weigh my client's 5.8-year, 1204-trip, 4.9-rated record with 0 disputes and 0 upheld (F8); profile facts can support a flag request but can never decide a case, and here there is nothing to flag.
